page: Microsoft Azure E2pds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an arm64 processor and managed through Microsoft Hyper-V. The hardware configuration provides 2 dedicated vCPUs paired with 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. Storage features include 118 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD capacity alongside support for Azure Premium Storage. The instance does not include discrete GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Operating on the 64-bit ARM architecture, the E2pds_v7 relies on native ARM execution environments without x86 vector or matrix extensions. Dedicated vCPU provisioning provides consistent compute execution without the resource variability found in shared or burstable environments. The onboard 118 GB NVMe SSD functions as high-throughput, low-latency temporary storage, while persistent state requires network-attached storage integration.

With its 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the instance emphasizes memory capacity and I/O responsiveness over raw multithreaded compute density. This profile yields a resource-efficient footprint for memory-bound applications, including in-memory key-value stores like Redis, small database instances, backend microservices, and web application caches.
description: Microsoft Azure E2pds_v7 is a memory-optimized cloud server instance built on 64-bit ARM architecture and running on Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs alongside 16.0 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per-core allocation ratio designed for memory-intensive operations. The instance integrates 118 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage and offers compatibility with Azure Premium Storage volumes, operating without discrete GPU accelerators. Because the processor utilizes the arm64 instruction set, workloads must be compiled for or natively support ARM. The presence of low-latency local NVMe storage provides rapid temporary data access, complementing the high memory-to-core balance. Delivering dedicated compute resources without shared-thread overhead, the E2pds_v7 is well aligned for lightweight in-memory caching solutions like Redis, small database deployments, backend microservices, and structured staging environments that prioritize memory capacity over extensive parallel compute capacity.
